title: Immutable Audit Indexing and Evidence Export for WORM-backed Admin Logs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Customers in regulated industries require immutable, auditable evidence for admin actions, configuration changes, and access events. Existing work (sealed/audit shipping, append-only archival) covered raw retention and integrity shipping, but we lack a cohesive, verifiable export pipeline and an immutable indexed catalog that auditors can query without exposing live systems.

Goal: Implement an end-to-end solution to store admin audit logs in WORM-backed storage, maintain an immutable indexed ledger for quick evidence discovery, and provide tamper-evident export bundles (signed manifests + NDJSON events) for auditors and legal requests. The solution must support per-customer residency and retention settings, KMS/HSM-backed signing, legal-hold exclusion from deletion, and automated evidence/reporting flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- All admin actions, access attempts, and config changes are written to a WORM-backed store (S3 Object Lock or equivalent) with object-level metadata including region and retention policy.
- An append-only index (immutable ledger) exists that maps events to WORM object IDs and stores SHA256 object digests; the ledger itself is verifiable and contains monotonic sequence numbers.
- Evidence export API generates a signed bundle containing: NDJSON event stream, manifest (SHA256 per-object, sequence ranges, export timestamp, residency tag), KMS/HSM signature, and verification instructions.
- Console and API surfaces allow tenant admins to configure data residency and retention windows (retention duration, legal hold), and to schedule periodic evidence exports.
- Automated monthly retention reports and one-click auditor exports are available; report generation latency under 10 minutes for exports spanning up to 30 days of events.
- Verification tooling (CLI and internal endpoint) validates bundle integrity and signature.
- End-to-end tests, benchmarks for export performance, and telemetry for export success/failure rates and time-to-first-byte.

Implementation approach:
1) Storage: use dedicated per-region, per-tenant WORM-enabled buckets (S3 object-lock compliance mode) or on-prem equivalent. Enforce server-side encryption and tenant-specific KMS keys where required by residency.
2) Indexing: append-only ledger stored in a write-once append pattern (e.g., Bigtable with time-ordered rows or a dedicated PostgreSQL append-only table with WAL snapshotting). Each ledger entry contains: sequence_id, event_time, event_type, resource_id, object_id, object_sha256, tenant_id, residency_region. Ledger rows are hashed into periodic Merkle roots to enable compact verification.
3) Signing & Integrity: integrate with KMS/HSM to sign export manifests. Signatures, public key metadata, and certificate chain are stored alongside bundle metadata (not in the live log).
4) Export pipeline: a dedicated export service will accept export requests (time range, tenant, residency), query ledger for object IDs, stream NDJSON events from WORM objects into a bundle, compute and persist manifest entries, and produce final signed archive (tar + manifest + signature) stored in a locked export bucket and made available via time-limited, auditable download links.
5) Console/UI: add a retention & residency page under Org Settings enabling: default retention policy, per-application overrides, legal hold toggle, and scheduled exports. Expose an "Generate Auditor Bundle" action with scope options.
6) Verification tooling: implement a CLI command (redwood audit verify <bundle>) and an internal verification endpoint for auditors that validates SHA256 digests and KMS signatures and returns a signed verification receipt.
7) Observability & SLOs: instrument export latency, bundle verification success, and unexpected object-not-found errors. Define SLO: 99% of exports for <30-day windows complete within 10 minutes.

Migration & Compatibility: Provide a migration path for existing archived audit logs: backfill index entries by scanning archival sinks and computing object SHA256; tag migrated objects with migration marker and ledger sequence numbers. During migration, exports must include a migration_notice file.

Privacy & Residency: retention settings must respect tenant residency selections; when generating bundles for auditors, export service must only assemble objects stored in the tenant's selected region unless explicit cross-region consent is present.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: Spike and prototype export pipeline with S3 Object Lock and KMS signing (done).
- Week 3-4: Implement append-only ledger service and Merkle checkpointing; build CLI verification tool.
- Week 5: Console surfaces for retention/residency and schedule exports.
- Week 6: End-to-end tests, performance tuning, legal review, and beta with 3 enterprise customers.
- Week 7: GA with docs & runbook.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Large exports could be heavy on IO: implement streaming NDJSON with backpressure and chunked manifest creation to avoid buffering big windows in memory.
- Key management complexity across regions: require tenant-scoped KMS keys and provide clear key-rotation docs; fallback signing keys for cross-region consent scenarios.
- Verification performance for large bundles: provide incremental verification (verify manifest chunks) and provide verifier memory/CPU guidance.

Open questions:
- Should ledger Merkle roots be published periodically to a public bulletin (for cross-tenant tamper evidence) or kept internal? (Legal leaning: internal only, but PM to confirm).
- Exact retention UI copy and allowed overrides for org admins vs tenant-specific settings.

Acceptance tests / QA checklist:
- Create audit events across hosts, trigger export, validate bundle integrity & signature with CLI.
- Attempt to delete WORM objects pre-retention: verify prevention and legal-hold behavior.
- Migrate 90 days of existing logs; verify exported bundle includes migration_notice and ledger continuity.
- Simulate KMS key rotation and ensure previously-signed manifests still verify using stored cert chain.

Deliverables:
- Export service implementation + tests, append-only ledger + Merkle checkpointing, Console retention/residency UI, verification CLI, runbook + legal sign-off, telemetry dashboards and SLIs.
